I’ll run `crimes scan --format json` and check the client and API code, then rank the mismatches by their production impact.


The source shows mismatches the scan missed: the read URL also uses `/workspaces`, two calls send literal `:id` values, and both write calls omit required inputs. The scan’s claim that unsupported plans are rejected also needs qualification: TypeScript types don’t validate responses, and the API accepts `plan` as a plain string.


Ran `crimes scan --format json` and checked all three source files. The scan reports five findings; source review reveals additional contract failures. Ranked by production impact:

1. **P1 — Workspace reads and creation hit nonexistent routes: 404.**  
   [getWorkspace, line 18](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:18) requests `GET /api/workspaces/{id}`, and `createWorkspace`, line 23, requests `POST /api/workspaces`. The API declares `/api/teams/{team_id}` and `/api/teams` in [routes.py, lines 10–16](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10). Both operations fail. The scan missed the concatenated GET URL.

2. **P1 — Plan changes use the wrong method: 405.**  
   [changeWorkspacePlan, line 34](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:34) sends `PUT`; [the API, line 25](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/api/billing/routes.py:25) only declares `POST`. Every attempt fails before reaching the handler.

3. **P1 — Creation omits a required request body: 422 after correcting the path.**  
   [createWorkspace, line 23](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:23) sends no body, while [create_team, line 16](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/api/billing/routes.py:16) requires `payload: dict`. Sending `{}` as JSON satisfies the current handler.

4. **P1 — Plan changes never send the selected plan: 422 after correcting the method.**  
   [changeWorkspacePlan, lines 33–34](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:33) ignores its `plan` argument. [change_team_plan, line 26](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/api/billing/routes.py:26) requires a **query parameter**, such as `?plan=pro`. Adding only a JSON body would still fail.

5. **P2 — Two calls send literal `:id` instead of the supplied ID.**  
   [workspaceSeats, line 28](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:28) and `changeWorkspacePlan`, line 34, ignore their `id` arguments. Fetch does no placeholder substitution. FastAPI accepts `:id` as the string `team_id`: the seats request currently returns `200 {"seats":1}`, silently concealing the mistake. After fixing the other plan-request defects, that handler returns `"id":":id"`.

6. **P2 — HTTP failures resolve as successful client results.**  
   All four functions in [workspace-client.ts](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:17) parse JSON without checking `res.ok`. Consequently, JSON 404/405/422 responses become resolved error objects masquerading as successful results. A seats error produces `undefined` despite its `Promise<number>` signature. This conceals the failures above from callers relying on promise rejection.

7. **P2 — Plan definitions disagree, and runtime validation is absent.**  
   [Python’s canonical enum](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10) contains `free | pro | team | scale`; [TypeScript](/private/var/folders/8_/6tdb3p2s63v_xxb15r46cqwr0000gn/T/crimes-eval-agent-v6pGeF/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10) contains `free | pro | enterprise`. Only `free` and `pro` agree. **The scanner overstates runtime rejection:** TypeScript does not validate incoming JSON, and the API handler accepts a plain `str`. A corrected request with `plan=enterprise` actually returns 200. The current read/create handlers always return `free`, so they do not yet expose `team` or `scale`.

8. **P3 — “Workspace” versus “team” obscures the shared concept.**  
   Client names and API names differ throughout these files. This increases maintenance risk and has already leaked into the broken URLs. Different internal names alone cause no runtime failure; document the mapping or standardize it.

The scanner’s `getWorkspace` “False Identity” finding is a false positive for this review: its fetch is a GET, and no mutation is evident.

Validated the status codes using the declared router in FastAPI 0.115.6’s TestClient, and captured requests from all four client functions. No source files changed.
